title: loopctl accepts a holder's offline events by idempotent id, fencing the late ones

story.as_a: holder that lost loopctl and has just reconnected
story.i_want_to: send everything I recorded while offline in one ordered replay, and learn per entry whether it applied, was already applied, or was fenced
story.so_that: nothing I recorded is applied twice or lost, and nothing I recorded after my claim ended overwrites the current holder's item

rationale: PRD R9 and section 7 point 1: a holder that loses loopctl finishes its lease, records events and checkpoints locally and replays them on reconnect; event ids are idempotent, so a replay never applies twice, and a lease that lapsed meanwhile fences the late events out of the item's state while its checkpoint is still kept, as a fenced checkpoint. Today a write at an ended claim is refused 409 stale_claim_epoch (lib/loopctl_web/fallback_controller.ex:270) and the caller's record is gone. Each work-item verb answers one write, so replaying through them one by one loses the per-sender order section 5 promises and drops every late write; one replay route that applies entries in the holder's order and stores late ones as fenced history closes both.

acceptance_criteria.description: POST /api/v1/holders/:id/replay (role :agent) takes {entries: [...]}, each entry {event_id, seq, kind, story_id, claim_epoch, recorded_at, payload} with kind note (a work-item note) or checkpoint, and applies the entries in ascending seq order, each in its own transaction.

The route answers 200 with results: one {event_id, outcome} per entry in seq order, outcome one of applied, replayed, fenced or refused, a refused entry carrying error.code; one entry's refusal never stops the entries after it.

An entry whose event_id the tenant already holds with an equal payload answers outcome replayed with the first application's result and writes nothing; with a different payload it answers refused, code event_id_conflict.

An entry whose claim_epoch is not the story's current claim_epoch, or whose holder is not stories.assigned_holder_id, changes no item state: a note is stored as a story_stage_events row with event fenced_replay (data: the entry's kind, payload, recorded_at, its epoch and the current one), and a checkpoint is stored in story_checkpoints with fenced true; the outcome is fenced.
The route answers 403 code holder_mismatch when the calling key's holder_id is not :id, so one holder can never replay as another.
A body whose seq values are not strictly increasing, or with more than @max_replay_entries (200) entries, is refused 422 replay_not_ordered or replay_too_large before any entry is applied.

A replayed entry and a current holder's write to the same story at the same moment serialize on the stage row lock: exactly one of them applies against the claim it read, and the other is applied after it or fenced, never both on stale state.
MCP tool holder_replay sends the entries with the holder credential and its description names the four outcomes, the 403 holder_mismatch and the two 422 codes.

test_cases.name: a replay applies in seq order and one refusal does not stop the rest (DataCase)
preconditions: tenant = fixture(:tenant); a story claimed by a holder (holder fixture provided by release 3) at claim_epoch 4
three entries at seq 1, 2, 3: a progress note, an entry with an unknown kind, a checkpoint at epoch 4
steps: Holders.replay(tenant.id, holder, entries) with the entries sent in order 3, 1, 2
expected_results: results in seq order: applied, refused (code invalid_entry), applied; the note precedes the checkpoint in the story's event log

test_cases.name: the same event_id twice is replayed, a changed payload is a conflict (DataCase)
steps: replay the same event_id with a different payload
expected_results: replayed with one note row in story_notes; refused event_id_conflict with still one row

test_cases.name: entries from an ended claim are kept as fenced history and change nothing (DataCase)
preconditions: holder A claimed the story at epoch 4; the lease was reclaimed by ReclaimExpiredClaimsWorker and holder B claimed it at epoch 5
steps: holder A replays a note and a checkpoint at epoch 4
expected_results: both fenced; story stage, assigned_holder_id and B's latest checkpoint unchanged; one fenced_replay event row and one story_checkpoints row with fenced true, each naming epochs 4 and 5

test_cases.name: role, holder and body refusals (ConnCase)
preconditions: holder credentials for holders A and B; a user key; an orchestrator key
steps: POST it with the user key and with the orchestrator key
expected_results: 403 holder_mismatch; 422 replay_not_ordered; 422 replay_too_large; each role refusal as the router's :agent pipeline answers it, and no row written in any case

test_cases.name: a replay racing the current holder's write (DataCase, async: false, two connections)
preconditions: Loopctl.Test.ProductionTopology; story held by B at epoch 5; A's replay entry at epoch 4
steps: Task 1 runs A's replay while Task 2 runs B's stage transition; both start on a barrier
expected_results: B's transition applied; A's entry fenced; the stage row's lock_version advanced once

test_cases.name: tenant isolation: a story id from another tenant is refused (DataCase)
preconditions: a story in tenant B; holder in tenant A
steps: Holders.replay(tenant_a.id, holder, [entry naming tenant B's story])
expected_results: refused, code not_found; no row in either tenant

test_cases.name: holder_replay wiring and description (node --test)
preconditions: mcp-server tool list and a fetch stub
expected_results: POST /api/v1/holders/<id>/replay with the entries verbatim; the description contains applied, replayed, fenced, refused, holder_mismatch, replay_not_ordered and replay_too_large

technical_notes: Why a new route: every existing work-item verb applies one write and refuses an ended claim with 409 stale_claim_epoch (FallbackController.call/2, lib/loopctl_web/fallback_controller.ex:270; StoryStatusController epoch checks at lib/loopctl_web/controllers/story_status_controller.ex:47,612), so a holder replaying through them loses its late writes and its order. The route lives in the holders controller release 3 creates (README names table: holder, holder credential) and reuses each verb's context function for an entry that is current; it adds no table.

Dedupe: each target row carries the entry's event_id under a unique index (README epic-wide rule: every write that can be retried carries an id). If release 3 or 7 left story_notes, story_stage_events or story_checkpoints without one, this story adds event_id and a (tenant_id, event_id) unique index; the conflict check compares the stored row's payload with the entry's.

story_stage_events: Loopctl.Delivery.StageEvent (lib/loopctl/delivery/stage_event.ex:40), fields :41-51 including claim_epoch :48. Its moduledoc event list (:6-26) is the story_stage_events_event CHECK allow-list (:27-29), so fenced_replay needs a migration rewriting that constraint and a line in the moduledoc.

Lock order: take the story FOR SHARE, then the stage row FOR UPDATE, as Loopctl.Delivery.Stages documents (lib/loopctl/delivery/stages.ex:78-84); the epoch and holder are compared under those locks, so a reclaim (Loopctl.Workers.ReclaimExpiredClaimsWorker, lib/loopctl/workers/reclaim_expired_claims_worker.ex:1) cannot commit between the check and the write.

story_checkpoints and its fenced flag are provided by release 7 (README names table: checkpoint); a fenced checkpoint is subject to the same diff bound as any checkpoint. stories.assigned_holder_id is provided by release 3 (README names table: the claim's holder).

@max_replay_entries is one module attribute read by the guard and the operation/2 spec (CLAUDE.md, Doc hygiene: new API constraint). 200 entries stays inside the 2 MB body limit (LoopctlWeb.RequestLimits @max_body_bytes, lib/loopctl_web/request_limits.ex:18) for notes and stage events; a client splits checkpoints across bodies.
recorded_at is the holder's clock, kept in the row's data for the timeline; ordering and state use seq and the server's inserted_at only.

MCP: mcp-server/lib/holders.js request shape, a declaration and case in mcp-server/index.js, a row in mcp-server/README.md, a wiring test (CLAUDE.md, An operator-facing endpoint is NOT DONE until an MCP tool calls it). The tool is what US-52.62's journal calls.
non_goals: Journaling writes while offline and replaying them on reconnect from the client: US-52.62.
Showing fenced_replay rows: the timeline from release 5 (README names table: visibility) lists every event row already.
Replaying a stage transition, move, claim or verify: each needs a live answer that decides the holder's next step, so none is journaled (US-52.62).

failure_modes.partition: AC-52.61.4: what a partitioned holder recorded after its lease was reclaimed is stored as fenced history and never applied over the new holder's state.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.61.4: every replayed entry ends as a row in loopctl's Postgres (applied, or a fenced_replay event, or a fenced checkpoint), so the holder's local journal can be deleted once it has a result for each entry.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.61.3: an entry's event_id is unique per tenant, so a second replay of it answers replayed and writes nothing.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.61.2: a replay that times out client-side is resent whole; the entries that committed answer replayed, so a slow connection costs a resend and never a double write.
failure_modes.reach: AC-52.61.7: the replay runs in the request process under the story and stage row locks every transition takes, so no queue or second process holds an entry.

definition_of_done: On production, in the end-to-end sandbox project: claim a story with holder A, cut A's network, let the lease lapse and holder B claim it, restore A and replay one note and one checkpoint; GET /api/v1/stories/:id/timeline shows both as fenced and B's head unchanged.
defaults: Replay outcome names: applied, replayed, fenced, refused.
